text:
priya: seeing weird memory growth on long-context streams, might be kvpage reuse bug. repro attached below.

priya: scenario: 50k token convo, multiple users multiplexed on same worker, after ~30k tokens mem climbs and we start getting stale token reads in later requests.

priya: minimal repro: run loadtest with --long-context and --request-id-per-call, then tail logs. i can share docker image.

mira: ugh. is this the same as the old alignment issue? any logs showing Owner/PrevOwner headers?

priya: here's a snippet from runtime log showing a suspicious page handoff: 

```
kv_page_alloc id=42 offset=32768 len=1024 owner=req=abc123 tag=0x1
kv_page_append id=42 offset=32768 len=128 owner=req=abc123
kv_page_free id=42 owner=req=abc123
kv_page_alloc id=42 offset=32768 len=1024 owner=req=def456 tag=0x0
kv_page_append id=42 offset=32768 len=64 owner=req=def456
kv_page_read id=42 offset=32704 len=64 owner=req=def456 observed_prev=req=abc123
```

priya: note the read offset 32704 is 64 bytes before offset, which maps to a previous append. looks like stale block read with wrong token alignment.

dan: can you paste the pid/worker id? i want to check page refcounting and if eviction raced with reuse.

prya: worker=worker-7 pid=4218, running dev build from commit 0f8a3c9 (merged yesterday).

ash: possible hypothesis: partial eviction moves last_page pointer but we reuse the slot before clearing the trailing bytes. if reader uses cached block length from previous owner, you get misaligned reads.

mira: that matches a repro i saw where batching + partial flush produced fragment reuse. also saw increase in fragmentation in pprof heap.

priya: i ran pprof heap at 30k tokens, looks like rising retained bytes in kv_pages:

```
# top 5 contributors
130MB  45%  kv_pages
80MB   28%  in-flight-request-objects
30MB   10%  kv_fragments
```

priya: but the growth is capped until we hit contamination, then it spikes.

ash: any recent kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes that could alter access pattern?

priya: batching tweak from commit e2d2f1c changed target batch size heuristics, increased average seq per request — more long-lived KV entries per worker.

simon: i can try reproducing locally. will add extra assertions to kv read path to check current owner tag vs observed_prev.

priya: i already added an invariant check and got failures: 

```
panic: kv_read observed prev_owner != zero and prev_owner != current_owner (prev=abc123 cur=def456)
stack: ...
```

mira: good. so root cause seems to be cross-request contamination when a page is freed and immediately reallocated to another request without zeroing. race between evict and append path.

dan: two options: (1) quick mitigation: tag pages with allocation epoch + verify on reads; (2) slower: zero-fill on alloc or move to a grace window before reuse.

ash: zero-fill hurts perf on hot path. epoch-tagging is cheap: include alloc_epoch in header and on read ensure block. but we need to guard against partial writes where new owner wrote only part.

priya: tag approach caught it consistently for me. i added a debug env var KV_DEBUG_STRICT=1 and we reproduced 8/8 runs.

kv-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/worker-7 will roll with debug build at 1857643300. monitor /alerts/kv-stale-blocks.

simon: created a test in runtime/test/kv_repro.cc that simulates interleaved free+alloc; failing. pushing patch with epoch-tagging + assert to my branch simon/kv-epoch-fix.

mira: also add unit to ensure evict path serializes with alloc or increments epoch under lock.

dan: assign to @simon and @ash to review. PR must include microbenchmark showing <5% perf regression under typical L2 workload.

priya: next steps: simon will open PR, ash reviews, dan + mira greenlight canary. i'll run long-run repro on canary two nights in a row.

ash: FYI I saw a potential regression introduced by e2d2f1c in our routing bench; will include baseline numbers in review.

priya: thanks all. recording this as follow-up for postmortem if we see more production hits. :thumbsup:
